elements.element: Customer-payable liquidated amount is limited to an early-termination fee
elements.evidence: "shall be the sole and exclusive amount payable by the Company in connection with such termination"

elements.element: Cap on that fee equal to 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "shall in no event exceed an amount equal to three (3) months' fees under Section 3.1"

elements.element: Stated as the sole liquidated amount (no other liquidated damages/penalties on termination)
elements.evidence: "the sole and exclusive amount payable by the Company in connection with such termination"

elements.element: No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer at all
elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" remains, merely capped

elements.element: Cap references an existing fee provision (no dangling cross-reference)
elements.evidence: "three (3) months' fees under Section 3.1" — Section 3.1 is not among the resolved definitions/extracts

offending_extra_words: (calculated using the average monthly fees payable during the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date)
reasons: The fallback bargain is satisfied on its material terms: the Termination Payment is capped at three months' fees and declared the sole amount payable on termination, so the clause now sits at our accepted fallback rather than in deviation territory.
The preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) is not met because the Net Sales–based Termination Payment formula survives; it is only limited by a proviso.

Minimality fails: the single edit expands a 9-word tail into 63 words (ratio 7.0, changed-character ratio 0.883). The average-monthly-fee computation gloss and the 'and exclusive ... in connection with such termination' verbiage go beyond the short cap-and-sole-amount phrase needed to complete the fallback.

The cross-reference to 'Section 3.1' cannot be verified from the supplied text; if that section does not state the fees, the cap mechanic dangles and should be replaced with a reference to fees actually payable under the Agreement.
Unrelated terms (the eight quarterly instalments in (c), the 90-day notice mechanic, the $800,000 deduction) are left intact and effective.
